neighbours.label: Whether a drug or treatment works: 'effective', 'efficacy', 'effectiveness' in medical text, not 'effective' in general
fire: The antibiotic proved safe and effective in most children.
Trials showed the vaccine's efficacy against severe disease.
Alcohol may lower the effectiveness of the medication.
This drug is ineffective for many patients with asthma.
Doctors doubt the long-term efficacy of the therapy.
The ointment is effective for treating mild eczema.
The study compared the effectiveness of two statins.
No evidence supports its efficacy for back pain.
quiet: The advertising proved clever and effective in most towns.
Polls showed the mayor's lead over his rival.
Alcohol may lower the price of the party.
This law took effect for many drivers in April.
Economists doubt the long-term effect of the tariff.
The poster is effective for selling mild salsa.
The study compared the cost of two statins.
No evidence supports the claim about back pain.

predictions: The medical sense fires. Effective advertising, 'took effect' and non-efficacy statements about the same drugs stay quiet.
